display_name: Sher Shah Suri & Shahu Sultan at Rohtas
one_line: Sher Shah Suri, Afghan emperor, and his officer Shahu Sultan supervising the frontier Rohtas Fort works near the Jhelum around 1541–1543 CE.

appearance.age_look: Sher Shah looks like a broad-shouldered man in his late 40s, Shahu Sultan a lean man in his mid-30s; both fit, with soldiers’ posture.
appearance.face: Sher Shah has a square face, wheatish complexion, strong nose, trimmed mustache and short beard, with calm commanding eyes and a thoughtful firm expression; Shahu Sultan has an oval face, slightly lighter wheatish skin, straight nose, neat mustache and stubble, with focused, attentive eyes and a respectful, alert expression.
appearance.hair: Sher Shah’s hair is hidden under a tall, slightly tapering Afghan-style turban in warm sand-beige with a dark green band and a subtle fold at the front; Shahu Sultan wears a smaller rounded turban in deep rust-red with a narrow beige wrap, both leaving no loose hair visible.
appearance.costume: Sher Shah wears a mid-16th-century North Indian-Afghan noble’s outfit: a long quilted jama-style robe in muted olive green reaching mid-calf, side-tied, with finely patterned darker green edging at the collar, cuffs and hem; beneath, a cream cotton tunic glimpses at the neckline, and he has straight, slightly loose trousers in soft beige, tucked into plain dark brown leather riding boots; over the jama is a broad dark brown leather belt with a metal buckle and small attached pouch, and a simple, narrow dark green sash tied at the left hip; his turban matches with sand-beige cloth and a dark green band, and he wears minimal jewellery—just a plain gold ring on his right hand. Shahu Sultan wears a practical officer’s costume: a knee-length straight-cut cotton jama in warm light brown with a faint, regular check pattern, cinched by a slim dark leather belt; under it, off-white trousers fall to the ankles, worn with sturdy brown leather shoes; over his shoulders is a sleeveless, slightly padded waistcoat in deep indigo blue, plain but visibly utilitarian; his rust-red turban is simply wrapped, and he wears no jewellery, emphasizing his working role at the site.
appearance.signature: Sher Shah carries a sheathed straight-bladed talwar at his left hip with a simple iron hilt and plain brown scabbard, his right hand often resting on its pommel; Shahu Sultan holds a rolled parchment site plan tied with a green cord in his left hand as his constant prop.

ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri is a wheatish, square-faced, bearded Afghan emperor in an olive green quilted jama, beige trousers, brown boots, sand-beige turban and talwar at his hip, beside Shahu Sultan in a brown checked jama, indigo waistcoat, rust-red turban, holding a rolled green-tied plan.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historical characters standing together at Rohtas Fort: Sher Shah Suri and Shahu Sultan. Sher Shah is a broad-shouldered, wheatish-complexioned man in his late 40s with a square face, strong nose, short trimmed beard and mustache, and calm commanding eyes. His hair is covered by a tall Afghan-style sand-beige turban with a dark green band and a subtle fold at the front. He wears a mid-16th-century North Indian-Afghan noble’s outfit: a long quilted jama-style robe in muted olive green reaching mid-calf, side-tied, with darker green patterned edging at collar, cuffs and hem, over a cream tunic barely visible at the neck. He has straight beige trousers tucked into plain dark brown leather riding boots, a broad dark brown leather belt with a metal buckle and small pouch, and a narrow dark green sash tied at his left hip. A simple straight-bladed talwar in a plain brown scabbard hangs at his left hip, and a single gold ring sits on his right hand. Beside him, Shahu Sultan is a lean officer in his mid-30s with an oval face, slightly lighter wheatish skin, neat mustache and stubble, and focused, respectful eyes. His hair is wrapped in a smaller rounded rust-red turban with a narrow beige wrap. He wears a knee-length light brown cotton jama with a faint check pattern, cinched by a slim dark leather belt, off-white trousers to the ankles, and sturdy brown leather shoes. Over his torso is a sleeveless deep indigo waistcoat, slightly padded and plain. In his left hand he always holds a rolled parchment site plan tied with a green cord. Show them front-facing, full-body, with clear views of faces, turbans, robes, belts, boots, waistcoat, talwar and plan, in clean, confident colors dominated by olive green, sand beige, dark brown, deep indigo blue and rust red.
